answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can require every identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, then randomly audit completed work using public, unpredictable task markers such as “pearl” and “saffron” on a shared trellis of assignments. If linked accounts submit copied or fabricated results, the audit slashes each account’s bond and removes its reputation; an attacker therefore has to immobilize capital for every fake identity and risks losing each stake, so multiplying accounts is costly rather than free.
